shortDescription: Provision new virtual machines using virt-install tool

options.name: arch
options.description: Request a non-native CPU architecture for the guest virtual machine. If omitted, the host CPU architecture will be used in the guest.

options.name: audio
options.description: Configure host audio output for the guest's sound hardware. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual audio backend properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: audio_devices
options.description: Configure multiple audio backends for the guest.

options.name: autostart
options.description: Set the autostart flag for a domain.

options.name: blkiotune
options.description: Tune block I/O policy for the domain process.

options.name: boot
options.description: Set the boot device priority for post-install configuration.

options.name: boot_opts
options.description: Additional options for boot configuration. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual boot options.

options.name: cdrom
options.description: ISO file or CDROM device to use for VM install media.

options.name: channel
options.description: Attach a communication channel device to connect the guest and host machine. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual channel properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: channel_devices
options.description: Configure multiple channel devices for the guest.

options.name: clock
options.description: Configure the clock for the guest.

options.name: cloud_init
options.description: Pass cloud-init metadata to the VM. A cloud-init NoCloud ISO file is generated, and attached to the VM as a CDROM device.

options.name: console
options.description: Connect a text console between the guest and host. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual console properties. Common properties include C(type) and C(target) for different console types. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: console_devices
options.description: Configure multiple console devices for the guest.

options.name: container
options.description: This guest should be a container type guest.

options.name: controller
options.description: Attach a controller device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual controller properties. Examples include C(type=usb,model=none) to disable USB, or C(type=scsi,model=virtio-scsi) for VirtIO SCSI. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: controller_devices
options.description: Configure multiple controller devices for the guest.

options.name: cpu
options.description: Configure the CPU model and CPU features exposed to the guest.

options.name: cputune
options.description: Tune CPU parameters for the guest.

options.name: destroy_on_exit
options.description: If set to V(true), the VM will be destroyed when the console window is exited.

options.name: disks
options.description: Specify the storage devices for the guest.

options.name: events
options.description: Specify events values for the guest.

options.name: extra_args
options.description: Additional kernel command line arguments to pass to the installer when performing a guest install with O(location).

options.name: features
options.description: Enable or disable certain machine features. The value should be a dictionary where each key is a feature name and the value is a dictionary of options for that feature. An empty object V({}) for a feature indicates to turn on that feature with default options. Example: V(hyperv.spinlocks: {state: off}), V(pvspinlock: {})

options.name: filesystems
options.description: Specifies directories on the host to export to the guest.

options.name: graphics
options.description: Configure the graphical display for the guest virtual machine. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual properties. Common properties include C(type) (e.g. V(vnc), V(spice)) and C(listen).

options.name: graphics_devices
options.description: Configure multiple graphics devices for the guest.

options.name: host_devices
options.description: Configure multiple host devices for the guest.

options.name: hostdev
options.description: Attach a physical host device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual host device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: hvm
options.description: Request the use of full virtualization.

options.name: idmap
options.description: Configure the UID or GID mapping for the guest.

options.name: import
options.description: Skip the OS installation process, and build a guest around an existing disk image.

options.name: initrd_inject
options.description: Add PATH to the root of the initrd fetched with O(location).

options.name: input
options.description: Attach an input device to the guest. Input device types include mouse, tablet, or keyboard. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual input device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: input_devices
options.description: Configure multiple input devices for the guest.

options.name: install
options.description: Additional options for the installation. This option is strictly for VM install operations, essentially configuring the first boot.

options.name: iommu
options.description: Add an IOMMU device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual IOMMU properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: iommu_devices
options.description: Configure multiple IOMMU devices for the guest.

options.name: iothreads
options.description: Number of I/O threads to configure for the guest.

options.name: iothreads_opts
options.description: Additional options for I/O threads configuration.

options.name: keywrap
options.description: Configure domain keywrap settings used for S390 cryptographic key management operations.

options.name: launch_security
options.description: Enable launch security for the guest.

options.name: location
options.description: The installation source, which can be a URL or a directory path containing the OS distribution installation media.

options.name: location_opts
options.description: Additional options for the installation source.

options.name: machine
options.description: The machine type to emulate. This will typically not need to be specified for Xen or KVM.

options.name: memballoon
options.description: Attach a virtual memory balloon device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual memory balloon properties. Common properties include C(model) (e.g. V(virtio), V(xen)). You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: memballoon_devices
options.description: Configure multiple memory balloon devices for the guest.

options.name: memory
options.description: Memory to allocate for the guest, in MiB.

options.name: memory_opts
options.description: Additional options for memory allocation.

options.name: memorybacking
options.description: Specify how virtual memory pages are backed by host pages

options.name: memtune
options.description: Tune memory policy for the domain process. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual memtune entries.

options.name: metadata
options.description: Specify the metadata for the guest virtual machine. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual metadata entries. e.g. V({uuid: 4dea22b3-1d52-d8f3-2516-782e98ab3fa0}) Use C(virt-install --metadata=?) to see a list of all available sub options.

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the new guest virtual machine instance.

options.name: networks
options.description: Connect the guest to the host network. Empty list V([]) means no default network interface.

options.name: noreboot
options.description: If set to V(true), the VM will not automatically reboot after the install has completed.

options.name: numatune
options.description: Tune NUMA policy for the domain process.

options.name: osinfo
options.description: Optimize the guest configuration for a specific operating system.

options.name: panic
options.description: Attach a panic notifier device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual panic device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: panic_devices
options.description: Configure multiple panic devices for the guest.

options.name: parallel
options.description: Attach a parallel device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual parallel device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: parallel_devices
options.description: Configure multiple parallel devices for the guest.

options.name: paravirt
options.description: This guest should be a paravirtualized guest.

options.name: pm
options.description: Configure the power management for the guest.

options.name: pxe
options.description: Install the guest from PXE.

options.name: qemu_commandline
options.description: Pass options directly to the qemu emulator. Only works for the libvirt qemu driver.

options.name: recreate
options.description: Use with present to force the re-creation of an existing VM.

options.name: redirdev
options.description: Add a redirected device for USB or other device redirection. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual redirection properties. Common properties include C(bus=usb), C(type=tcp) or C(type=spicevmc). You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: redirected_devices
options.description: Configure multiple redirected devices for the guest.

options.name: resource
options.description: Specify resource partitioning for the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual resource entries. Use C(virt-install --resource=?) to see a list of all available sub options.

options.name: rng
options.description: Configure a virtual random number generator (RNG) device. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual RNG properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: rng_devices
options.description: Configure multiple RNG devices for the guest.

options.name: security
options.description: Configure domain seclabel domain settings. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual security entries.

options.name: serial
options.description: Attach a serial device to the guest with various redirection options. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual serial device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: serial_devices
options.description: Configure multiple serial devices for the guest.

options.name: shmem
options.description: Attach a shared memory device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual shared memory properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: shmem_devices
options.description: Configure multiple shared memory devices for the guest.

options.name: smartcard
options.description: Configure a virtual smartcard device. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual smartcard properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: smartcard_devices
options.description: Configure multiple smartcard devices for the guest.

options.name: sound
options.description: Attach a virtual audio device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual sound device properties. Common properties include C(model) (e.g. V(ich6), V(ich9), V(ac97)). You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: sound_devices
options.description: Configure multiple sound devices for the guest.

options.name: state
options.description: If set to V(present), create the VM if it does not exist. If set to V(absent), remove the VM if it exists.

options.name: sysinfo
options.description: Configure sysinfo/SMBIOS values exposed to the VM OS. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual sysinfo entries. Use C(virt-install --sysinfo=?) to see a list of all available sub options.

options.name: tpm
options.description: Configure a virtual TPM (Trusted Platform Module) device. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual TPM properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: tpm_devices
options.description: Configure multiple TPM devices for the guest.

options.name: transient
options.description: If set to V(true), libvirt forgets the XML configuration of the VM after shutdown or host restart.

options.name: unattended
options.description: Perform an unattended install using libosinfo's install script support.

options.name: uri
options.description: Libvirt connection uri.

options.name: vcpus
options.description: Number of virtual cpus to configure for the guest.

options.name: vcpus_opts
options.description: Additional options for virtual CPU configuration.

options.name: video
options.description: Specify what video device model will be attached to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual video device properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: video_devices
options.description: Configure multiple video devices for the guest.

options.name: virt_type
options.description: The hypervisor used to create the VM guest. Example choices are V(kvm), V(qemu), or V(xen).

options.name: vsock
options.description: Configure a vsock host/guest interface. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual vsock properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: vsock_devices
options.description: Configure multiple vsock devices for the guest.

options.name: wait_timeout
options.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the install to complete (rounded up to the nearest whole minute when passed to C(virt-install --wait)). When unset, the module will not pass C(--wait) to C(virt-install) and will start the install then exit (the module always uses C(--noautoconsole)). Use this for multi-phase unattended installs that reboot into a final post-install phase.

options.name: watchdog
options.description: Attach a virtual hardware watchdog device to the guest. The dictionary contains key/value pairs that define individual watchdog properties. You can use the special attribute C(value) to specify a primary value that appears before other properties in the command line.

options.name: watchdog_devices
options.description: Configure multiple watchdog devices for the guest.
